sections.label: Ministerial Statement on River Valley death
sections.summary: A Ministerial Statement will address questions about the death of a 13-year-old River Valley High School student on 19 July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Given significant public interest, today’s Ministerial Statement will also address those questions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Should their queries be sufficiently addressed, it may not be necessary for them to proceed with their PQs for the future Sittings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On 19 July, a 13-year-old student at River Valley High School died.

sections.label: Police custody and murder charge
sections.summary: Police arrived within 10 minutes, took a 16-year-old into custody, and he was charged with murder on 20 July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Upon receiving the call for assistance, Police arrived within 10 minutes and took the 16-year-old student into custody.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Preliminary investigations revealed that the two students had not known each other before the incident and the axe was purchased online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The 16-year-old student was charged in Court for murder the next day, on 20 July.

sections.label: MOE CARE officers and counsellors
sections.summary: Since last Wednesday, 98 MOE CARE officers and school counsellors have provided support at the CARE Post.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Since last Wednesday, a total of 98 MOE CARE officers and school counsellors, trained in psychological first aid and trauma management, have put aside their regular duties to provide much needed support at the CARE Post.

sections.label: CARE Post support numbers
sections.summary: About 540 staff and students have sought support at the CARE Post since it opened in the school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Since the CARE Post was opened in the school, about 540 staff and students have sought support there.

sections.label: Revised CCE curriculum implementation
sections.summary: This year, implementation of the revised CCE curriculum began with lower secondary levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I will then touch on the whole-of-society efforts we need to support our younger generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This year, we began implementing the revised CCE curriculum, starting with lower secondary levels.

sections.label: School peer support system
sections.summary: All schools are putting in place a peer support system to encourage students to look out for one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: All our schools are putting in place a peer support system to encourage students to look out for one another.

sections.label: School counsellor referrals to professionals
sections.summary: School counsellors refer students needing further intervention to professionals such as REACH teams or social service agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: When students need further intervention and help to access resources in the community, school counsellors refer them to professionals, such as those in the Response, Early intervention and Assessment in Community Mental Health (REACH) teams or social service agencies.

sections.label: Activities for young people's development
sections.summary: These activities help young people build bonds and grow emotionally, physically and psychologically, and will be reinstated fully when COVID-19 allows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: These activities are avenues for our young people to build bonds and to grow up in a balanced way, emotionally, physically and psychologically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We plan to reinstate such activities in full as soon as the COVID-19 situation allows for it.

sections.label: Teacher mental health training and counsellors
sections.summary: All teachers will receive enhanced professional development on mental health literacy, and more than 1,000 teacher counsellors will be deployed in the next few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: All teachers will receive enhanced professional development on mental health literacy as a baseline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This will further strengthen our ability to identify and support students in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We also aim to deploy more than 1,000 teacher counsellors in the next few years.

sections.label: Return of CCAs for students
sections.summary: CCAs for secondary schools and pre-universities will return within the next few weeks as more students complete their vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For our students, we will bring back CCAs for secondary schools and pre-universities within the next few weeks, as more students complete their vaccinations.

sections.label: Removal of Common Last Topics
sections.summary: Common Last Topics will be removed from the 2021 GCE O, N and A level examinations due to COVID-19 disruptions affecting students' well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Next, because of the disruptions to learning caused by COVID-19, we will remove the Common Last Topics (CLT) from the 2021 GCE examinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Delta variant of the COVID-19 virus has created much greater disruptions than envisaged and has affected the social and emotional well-being of our students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We are especially concerned for the graduating cohorts, so we will also remove the CLT from the 2021 GCE "O", "N" and "A" level examinations.

sections.label: Parent Support Groups mental well-being
sections.summary: MOE wants to strengthen partnership with parents through Parent Support Groups, encouraging each to form a sub-group focusing on mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: To this end, MOE wants to strengthen our partnership with parents through the Parent Support Groups in all our schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We hope that Parent Support Groups will not only support the school, but also expand their role to connect with one another and render help to parents whose children and families need more support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I will encourage every Parent Support Group to form a sub-group, focusing on the mental well-being of our children and families.

sections.label: School security measures and trust
sections.summary: The passage states that schools are a trusted space and that various security measures have been implemented in schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And above all, it is a trusted space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We have implemented various security measures in schools.

sections.label: MOE updating school security measures
sections.summary: MOE will continue updating security measures in a targeted and sensitive manner to balance security needs with safety, trust and homeliness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE will continue to update our security measures in a targeted manner and apply them sensitively to balance the security needs without losing our sense of safety, trust and homeliness of the school environment.

sections.label: Strengthening support for youths
sections.summary: The passage states such an incident could happen anytime and anywhere, so support for youths must be strengthened on three fronts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Such an incident could happen anytime and anywhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Therefore, we must strengthen support for our youths on three fronts: schools, family and the society at large.

sections.label: School counsellors and student referrals
sections.summary: School counsellors are deployed at every school, and students needing further intervention are referred to medical professionals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: School counsellors, who are specialised personnel providing dedicated counselling, are deployed at every school to meet the needs of students who require additional support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If students need further intervention, they are referred to medical professionals to ensure that they receive the necessary care.

sections.label: Care and community vigilance
sections.summary: The passage states the real key to staying safe lies in showing care for one another and enhanced community vigilance, not more intrusive security measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The real key to staying safe lies not with more intrusive security measures, but in showing care for one another and enhanced community vigilance.

sections.label: Run-Hide-Tell and teacher response
sections.summary: Students executed the Run-Hide-Tell steps as trained, and teachers responded swiftly, engaging the 16-year-old while prioritising student safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The students executed the “Run-Hide-Tell” steps exactly as they were trained to do in times of emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The teachers responded swiftly, demonstrating courage when engaging the 16-year-old and keeping the safety of their students as their utmost priority throughout.

sections.label: MOE support for students with mental health issues
sections.summary: Asks whether MOE will sensitise educators to students who are patients at IMH, public child guidance clinics and private hospitals, and consider regular student stress surveys.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Second, in light of this incident, whether MOE will take cognisance of students who are patients at IMH or even various public sector child guidance clinics, including those seeking psychiatric treatment, for example, at private hospitals and clinics, so that the educators will be sensitised and better prepared to support and prevent trigger events?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Thirdly, whether MOE can consider doing regular surveys with students at all levels to assess their stress levels and also the challenges they face growing up and, especially, if they are depressed?

sections.label: Decision to continue school after incident
sections.summary: School continued on Wednesday while allowing students and staff needing additional support or time to grieve to take leave of absence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the first issue of a time-out for the school, we had considered this and discussed with our professional colleagues if this was the best way for us to manage the incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But we also recognise that some students and staff may need additional support or may wish to have time and space to make sense of what has happened and grieve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That was why we adopted the posture to continue school on Wednesday, while allowing those who require the additional support to take leave of absence away from school.

sections.label: Regular check-ins with students and staff
sections.summary: MOE wants to institute regular check-ins with students and staff so they know where to go and how to manage when they need help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the third question that Mr Patrick Tay asked, yes, that is why we want to institute regular check-ins with our students and staff to make sure that if and when they need help, they know where to go, they know how to manage the situation.

sections.label: School security preparedness drills and initiatives
sections.summary: Asks what security preparedness drills and initiatives schools are equipped with, while not wanting schools made into fortresses.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The security within our schools goes a long way in instilling confidence in our students, parents, teachers and staff.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, my first clarification is, while we do not want schools to be made into fortresses, what security preparedness drills and initiatives are our schools equipped with?

sections.label: Avoiding stigmatisation in school mental health
sections.summary: Asks how the Ministry will ensure its relook into mental health in schools does not increase stigmatisation and prevent people from asking for help.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We want our students, teachers and staff to be able to easily and readily step forward to receive support whenever they need it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thus, my second clarification is, how would the Ministry ensure that while we relook into mental health in schools and the approaches that we are going to take, it does not increase the stigmatisation and prevent people from stepping forward and asking for help?

sections.label: Student drills for terrorist incidents
sections.summary: States that when drills were done with students, the baseline scenario was a terrorist incident, an external threat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the drills for the students, when we did the drills with the students, the baseline scenario was in the event of a terrorist incident, an external threat.

sections.label: Teacher security incident training
sections.summary: The speaker says more teachers will be cross-trained in security incident management so every school can respond adequately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I have discussed with my school principals as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We would, of course, like to have more of our teachers cross-trained in security incident management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And going forward, we will want to expand the group of people who are trained in such incident management so that every school can have the confidence to respond adequately should such an incident happen.

sections.label: Bringing back CCAs
sections.summary: Despite COVID-19, CCAs for older students will return as soon as possible to build social bonds and resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Despite COVID-19, we want to bring back CCAs for the older students as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is part of the process for them to build social bonds and to develop their emotional and psychological resilience; and we will do this as soon as we can.

sections.label: Confidentiality of medical records
sections.summary: The speaker assures that medical-in-confidence information of those seeking help is respected and not passed to other agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: But I will speak in more general terms of how we deal with the medical records of people who seek help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: I would just like to assure everyone that when someone comes forward to seek help, we respect the medical-in-confidence information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This will not be passed around to different agencies.

sections.label: Whole-of-nation approach message
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a whole-of-nation approach and asks Members to help spread the message that it is okay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the second issue, indeed, that is why, today, we make a call for us to adopt a whole-of-nation approach, for all of us as Members of this House to go forth and help us spread this message, that it is okay.

sections.label: Scoping down major examinations
sections.summary: The speaker is heartened the Minister took a decisive step to decelerate and scope down major examinations to prioritise mental health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is an ongoing challenge that we must all undertake together as a community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Minister has taken a very decisive step, amidst this tragedy, a step to decelerate the pace and to scope down on our major examinations when it is needed to prioritise the mental health of our students and teachers.

sections.label: Counselling waitlist and teacher workload
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether 540 help-seekers and 98 counsellors will cause waitlists, and what support teachers under extra workload get.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the Minister mentioned earlier that 540 students or individuals have sought help in the wake of this incident at River Valley High School.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that there are 98 counsellors available, would this actually lead to a waitlist?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, I understand that there might be a couple of months of waiting list for counselling services or mental health support services at Universities like NUS.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And then, finally, just a word on the workload of teachers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I understand that a lot of teachers are feeling very stressed out because, apart from teaching curriculum, making sure that they are giving the counselling for careers, they are now also expected to look out for their students' well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is a good thing, but I just wanted to know what sort of support is going to be given and available to teachers to make sure that they themselves are not stressed by the extra workload?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We also agree and we hope that the House will help us spread this message: not every distressed individual is a violent individual.

sections.label: CCE curriculum review and triage
sections.summary: MOE will continue updating the rest of the CCE curriculum, including primary schools, and a protocol triages students' and staff needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, having done the review of the CCE curriculum, for the secondary schools – and in the process of implementing it – MOE will continue to comb through and update the rest of the CCE curriculum, including for the Primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Third, yes, while over 500 have come forward to seek help, I want to share with Members that not all 500 require the same level of intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: And that is why there is a protocol for us in the system to triage the needs of both the students and the staff.

sections.label: Triage system and River Valley incident
sections.summary: The system triages individuals to get appropriate help, and in the River Valley High School incident students' and staff well-being is the concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This is how we work the system to triage to make sure that the respective individuals get the appropriate level of help for them to overcome their challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: That is why, in the River Valley High School incident, we are most concerned with both the mental well-being of our students and staff.

sections.label: MOE stance on behaviour
sections.summary: MOE states it does not stand for such behaviour in its schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: MOE's stance is very clear: we do not stand for such behaviour in our schools.

sections.label: Pandemic stress and CCE suggestion
sections.summary: A Member notes common last topics are removed to ease exam stress and suggests starting mental health literacy in Primary 6 with parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This pandemic has brought much stress to our students, especially those who are taking their major exams this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is heartening to note from the Minister's speech that to alleviate these students' stress and revision loads, the common last topics for PSLE, GCE "N", "O", "A" levels, will be removed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I also understand from what the Minister had shared earlier in relation to strengthening the social-emotional skills amongst our students, the CCE curriculum on mental health literacy has been introduced for lower secondary levels and it is in the midst of reviewing for Primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this aspect, I wish to suggest or recommend that, perhaps, it is the right juncture to consider implementing it, for a start, for our Primary 6 students onwards and also involving their parents' participation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I recall during a motivational talk which I conducted last year in my capacity as a school advisory chairman – I have been doing such talks for the past few years for Primary 6 students – unlike the previous batches, this batch of students looked pretty worried.

sections.label: Suicides among boys aged 10 to 19
sections.summary: Last year the number of suicides among boys aged 10 to 19 was at a record high.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last year, the number of suicides among boys aged 10 to 19 was at a record high.

sections.label: Tracking students' mental health
sections.summary: Today, students' mental health is tracked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, yes, today, we do track our students' mental health.

sections.label: Building trust with youths
sections.summary: Surveys and questionnaires can help, but building a relationship of trust lets youths seek help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Surveys, questionnaires can be helpful, but beyond looking at trends, I think we need to build a relationship of trust that can allow our youths to seek help.

sections.label: Specialised school staff functions
sections.summary: Schools now have teachers, teacher-counsellors, counsellors and managers so people specialise in functions rather than teachers carrying all workload.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At the same time, the way we are structuring the work in the school now is that there are teachers, there are also teacher-counsellors, there are also counsellors and there are also operational managers, admin managers, so that certain people specialise in certain functions, rather than exactly like what was suggested that, perhaps, many, many years ago, that we would put all this workload – from administration to operations to teaching to counselling – all on the shoulders of our teachers.

sections.label: Sympathetic school transfer requests
sections.summary: Requests for transfer of school will be looked at sympathetically and compassionately, especially if it improves the child's well-being.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, I would like to reassure Mr Liang Eng Hwa that we will certainly look at all requests for transfer of school sympathetically, compassionately, especially if it helps us to improve the well-being of the child.

sections.label: School counsellors deployment numbers
sections.summary: School counsellors have no teaching responsibilities; every school has at least one, over 1,000 are trained and about 700 deployed as teacher-counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: School counsellors are dedicated counsellors who have no teaching responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: At this point in time, every school has at least one school counsellor; some have more because of their higher needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In total, in the system today, we have trained more than 1,000 but we have deployed about 700 of them as teacher-counsellors because part of it is the posting cycle.

sections.label: Classrooms that lock from inside
sections.summary: Not all schools have classrooms that lock from the inside; newer, upgraded or renovated schools have them, and the rest will progressively follow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Today, at this point in time, not all schools have classrooms where they can lock from the inside.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The newer schools, those which have undergone the upgrading programme or the renovation programme, have already done this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will progressively do so for the remaining schools.

sections.label: Teacher training in student support
sections.summary: At NIE trainee teachers learn to build trust and spot distress signs, and some later train as teacher-counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First, in pre-service training at NIE, we equip all our trainee teachers with the basic modules of how to help their students by building a relationship of trust so that the students can confide in their teachers if they need help; how to look out for tell-tale signs whereby a student might be distressed, either in school or via events outside school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Once the teachers are in service, some of them will volunteer and some of them will be identified to take on additional training to become teacher-counsellors.

sections.label: Working with parents, school counsellors
sections.summary: Educators will be equipped to work with parents, and school counsellors are identified in two ways at the next level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: They will also be equipped to see how they can work with parents because working with parents is key to this whole journey of ours to provide the best support for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Then, at the next level, there are two ways which we identify school counsellors.

sections.label: MOE within whole-of-society system
sections.summary: MOE's work is part of a larger whole-of-society system involving MOH and MSF, building a community of support at different levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Having said that, what we can do within the MOE system is also part of a larger whole-of-society system, where MOH and MSF also come into play, so that, together, we build a community of support with different capacities at different levels to allow us to apply the appropriate help to the individuals in distress.

sections.label: Strife for excellence and comparison
sections.summary: The strive for excellence to better oneself must not become success defined in someone else's image or unrelenting comparison with others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: You must be very careful that this strife for excellence to better themselves does not turn into a situation where the definition of success is dictated in someone else's image; that it is an incessant and unrelenting comparison with somebody else.

sections.label: Care for two families
sections.summary: Care and support are being extended to the two families of the two children at the heart of the incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: My heart goes out to the parents and family members of the two children at the heart of the incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, we are, indeed, extending our care and support to the two families.

sections.label: Support for affected educators
sections.summary: The speaker is heartened that support is being provided now for educators affected by this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It took us all a while to get through that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I am heartened to hear the Minister say that there is support being provided right now for our educators who are affected by this.

sections.label: Whole-of-society approach, communal safety net
sections.summary: The question notes the Minister spoke of a whole-of-society approach and used the phrase communal safety net.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My question is: the Minister had talked about a whole-of-society approach and the Minister used the phrase "communal safety net".

sections.label: Supporting and trusting children
sections.summary: The passage calls on everyone and parents to take small steps, listen to younger ones, and give children assurance, confidence, trust and love.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: If we all can take small steps to look out for our younger ones, to give them a listening ear, to help them grow up in their own ways, find their footing; if all of us, as parents, can come together and give our children the assurance and the confidence that we believe in them, trust them and love them in spite of, so that our children will grow up confident in themselves and confident that, in any setback, they will have someone beside them.

sections.label: Grace at River Valley High
sections.summary: The passage states that in a moment of darkness, the speaker saw grace, compassion and solidarity among River Valley High School students and staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In that moment of darkness, I saw grace, I saw compassion, I saw solidarity amongst the students and staff of River Valley High School.
